title: Pick the deck's visual world
question: Four formats for the minimal deck, each drawn on a real slide. The roll assigned Kitchen Order Ticket. Keep it, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Kitchen Order Ticket
options.lineage: thermal KOT slips on a restaurant pass
options.thesis: Every slide is one order slip: the intent you hand the kitchen, because an agent will cook.
options.viewport: Paper slide, a small mono ticket header (order no., time, section), one dashed rule, the headline huge in a condensed grotesk, nothing else.
options.risk: If the ticket chrome creeps beyond the header line it turns into a costume.

raised.raise: Two type sizes in the whole deck; rank comes from empty space, not from size steps.
A strict five-step ink ramp is the only greys allowed; no tints, no shadows.
/btw slides sit as a second ticket clipped beneath the first, depth as aside.
Memes become numbered plates, FIG. 01 to 06, printed 1-bit by Codex.
Section openers are mostly blank ticket stock, a deep gap before each part.

options.label: Request for Comments
options.thesis: The talk as a spec: intent is an engineering artefact, so the deck reads like one.
options.viewport: Running head 'GrowthX Working Group · Oct 2026', headline in a grotesk, MUST/SHOULD in caps, footer '[Slide 4]'.
options.risk: The most familiar engineer aesthetic; many dev talks already look like this.

options.label: Object Poster
options.thesis: Section openers are saturated sheets with one flat object, content slides stay plain paper.
options.viewport: Ox-blood sheet, one flat terminal-window emblem drawn huge, section title cut beneath in a slab alphabet.
options.case: Strongest on clarity, one idea per slide at room scale; the room does not know the tradition.
options.risk: Color-heavy openers fight the 'minimal' ask if used on more than the ten section slides.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Slides as frames strung on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: Orange grain field, slide content in a punched white window.
options.case: Film editing is not this room's world, and orange on black fights minimal.
options.kept: One type size, rank by space.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Stacked translucent sheets over a zone ramp.
options.viewport: Hatched overlays across a tonal wedge.
options.case: Hatching and overlays add exactly the noise the brief removes.
options.kept: A strict tonal ramp as the only greys.

options.label: Sticker Accretion
options.thesis: Layers of half-covered stickers as chronology.
options.case: The opposite of minimal and of legible.

options.label: Curved Crease
options.thesis: A layout ruled by one sweeping arc.
options.viewport: Cream disc lifted along a charcoal arc.
options.case: No tie to the audience or to the talk's argument.
options.risk: Decorative geometry with nothing to say.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Content cut from blocks of cloud.
options.viewport: Cumulus cliff with blue voids between sections.
options.case: Surreal imagery steals the room from the speaker.

canonCard.label: Keynote minimal
canonCard.thesis: White slide, one huge black sans line, one accent, centered. What every minimal talk ships.
canonCard.viewport: One centered sentence at 96px, nothing else on screen.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other conference deck by design.
